extracted.intended_audience: prospective authors and reviewers for UAI 2025 (machine learning / uncertainty in AI researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and submission guidance for papers to the UAI 2025 conference, specifying the core review criteria, reproducibility expectations, and review process notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: The soundness and validity of the research methodology and findings

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: The originality and innovation of the contribution to the field

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: The quality and readability of the paper's presentation

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (encouraged)
rubrics_metrics.description: The conference encourages authors to enhance their submissions by making code and data publicly available, which supports reproducibility and strengthens the overall contribution to the research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making code/data public is encouraged and strengthens a submission, but is not stated as mandatory. Public artifacts can help back up claims and improve reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Process: double-blind and primary reliance on main paper
rubrics_metrics.description: UAI uses a double-blind review process via OpenReview. Reviewers are under no obligation to look at supplementary materials and base reviews primarily on the main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure the main paper is self-contained and presents key evidence and arguments clearly, because supplementary materials may not be read by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application-focused submissions: appropriate criteria and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Application-focused submissions are reviewed according to appropriate criteria and by reviewers with appropriate backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitting application-oriented work, expect reviewers to assess it with domain-appropriate standards; authors should highlight application-specific contributions and evaluation details to help matching and assessment.
